title: The Hidden Life of Embeddings: Linus Lee
talk_summary: Linus Lee demos encoder-decoder embedding models that reconstruct text from embeddings and allow latent-space arithmetic (length, sentiment, style, image interpolation). The core message is that making model internals visible and manipulable builds intuition, but the techniques are research prototypes, not production agent-engineering practices.

takeaways.what_they_do: They train a decoder to reconstruct text from embeddings, then project embeddings onto discovered directions (length, sentiment) to read out what a model 'sees' in an input.
takeaways.evidence_quote: embeddings show us what the model sees in a sample of input

takeaways.technique: Embedding reconstruction as a compression sanity check
takeaways.what_they_do: They show a 248-dim embedding can reconstruct most of a sentence including proper nouns, and even OpenAI Ada embeddings retain surprising detail via a linear adapter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's a surprising amount of detail that we've recovered out of just the embedding

takeaways.what_they_do: They add/subtract embedding vectors (e.g., 'sad crying man' minus 'smiling man') with normalization and scaling to steer generation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the only thing I'm doing is calculating vectors calculating embeddings for examples and uh and embedding them and just adding them together
